evidence:
The row-30 rule requires a matching success control for each absence check. Most frozen checks meet it: functional input/role/tier/anonymous/stale rows explicitly require the matching successful request, render pairs bad-password refusal with successful sign-in, and signing/equity caps require partial settlement. However, under .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/task/, tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:497,551,596 (hro_relocation_approval, hro_relocation_revision, hro_relocation_rescission) require successful status/input-changing operations and no relocation postings, but do not require an actual working nonzero payment/remittance for that action family. Line 497 says ?A successful approval is required?; line 551 requires ?Successful revisions that actually save the changed relocation inputs?; line 596 says ?Successful rescission is required?. The existence of a nonzero bonus input does not prove the payment writer works. The same file:974 explicitly supplies the missing kind of control for the coordinated equivalent: ?Use ordinary nonzero signing adjustments as the working-payment control?. Functional prompt.md:11,19,34 requires independent facts and says to score relocation exclusion independently; a signing/clawback sibling failure therefore cannot rescue these omitted controls. Public rules:139-141 exclude relocation from settlement while :226-227,:243-247,:265-269 require ordinary signing/remittance effects.

Measured local witness: qc/runs/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/per-row-review/evidence/30/payment-control-results.json (SHA256 b20a193e7e19d9577447d290fc1df9104c845f96275781657445bc39433c09ad) completes the same UI approval, two revisions, Finance rescission and new Auditor sign-in on the frozen golden and on a disposable copy with only remit() replaced by a no-op. Golden payment counts were 1/2/3/4; mutant counts remained 0/0/0/0, while it saved COMMITTED successors, relocation 12345/22222/33300 cents and final RESCINDED status. This confirms the concrete dead-payment behavior; the conclusion that these source bars admit its absence observations is reviewer analysis, not a measured judge grade. Driver SHA256 632bfed7cbdf4fa1a1f7cbd173b6a982c2964a6904981710698176213d7c3dbc; exact mutation diff SHA256 7e6655b58f4babfb0c681ac8b7999eda1ceaa7b2b2d658ac2e3bd27b36be0728; command record SHA256 2a17d97766da4183dd658eb19e9e43850301b7964f7c4f17218b55f089d5587b. Source mount was read-only, 13 frozen app hashes were verified unchanged, and network was disabled. Two driver errors are retained in attempt1/attempt2; neither is an app-failure finding.

Raw-evidence-index.json SHA256 1ef29f836bb775ef2ed19fc158bee979aef4d43ead0578fdb13fe9bacb6daad1: all 292 indexed artifact hashes verified. The cited targeted-golden browser results are bound to 14 matching frozen solution-file hashes and show a functioning golden signing display; they do not cover a disabled payment writer. Full configured judge/Oracle/model grading is absent and is not claimed. This verdict addresses only row 30.
counterexample: A working offer desk uses the ordinary frozen lifecycle but its remit() writer silently drops every signing payment, revision adjustment and rescission contra. Approval and both revisions still persist their statuses, lineage, terms, commitments and grants; rescission still persists its status/release. All three relocation-only negative bars see successful actions and zero relocation rows, even though the matching payment mechanism is dead. The isolated UI witness exhibits this exact behavior. Conforming alternative considered: an implementation may omit legitimate zero-valued remittance/adjustment/contra rows and use different labels/schema. Requiring any payment row after every action would falsely reject that alternative; the needed control is a demonstrably nonzero signing operation of the relevant action family, not a zero-row requirement or exact arithmetic verdict.
suggested_fix: Within each ordinary relocation exclusion criterion, require and reuse an actually observed nonzero signing remittance, signed adjustment or partially-unvested signing contra for the matching action family before awarding absence credit, while leaving exact amounts, zero-row omission, labels and sibling verdicts independent.
